scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which is outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Tyrone Jackson and I'm 31. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?
Okay, I see. Can you give me your account number so I can look at the subscription?
Sure, it's 8829-4401-X. Like I said, I canceled it, but the charge went through anyway.
Right. So, you canceled 34 days ago? That's past our 30-day window. I can't really do anything about that.
I understand the policy, but given that I was traveling and it was only a few days over, is there any exception you can make?
I don't know, I guess I can send this to the billing department. They handle the exceptions. What was your account number again?
It's 8829-4401-X, I just gave that to you a second ago. Is there really no one else who can help?
Yeah, I'm just going to escalate this to the billing team. They'll review it and get back to you. I've opened a case for you.

escalation_reason: Agent failed to exercise discretionary authority for a minor policy exception and instead pushed the request to the billing department.

judge_scores.justification: The agent demonstrated poor efficiency by asking for the customer's account number a second time after it was already provided. Furthermore, the agent showed minimal resolution effort and inappropriate escalation by immediately passing a minor, borderline exception request to the billing department without attempting to use their own authority.
